title: The Goodbye Room
evidence_boundary: Adapted from Earthwalker's December 8, 2015 DMT-Nexus self-report involving changa. The account is unverified personal testimony, not evidence of contact with the dead. The house, room, doors, and guarded love are original metaphors. Stock actors and places illustrate the account and do not depict its author or his wife.
grounding: The final six beats return to ordinary sounds, feet on the floor, breath, memories, and an open viewer question.
invitation: If your unfinished goodbye had a room, what would you want to say inside it?
end_card_question: If your unfinished goodbye had a room, what would you want to say inside it?
voice_standard: Liam: warm, intimate, reflective, a sly brilliant friend at midnight; gentle grief without melodrama. Sparse whisper directions only; captions contain narration, never performance tags.

scenes.text: He said he saw his wife during a DMT experience. She had died months earlier.
scenes.visual: colorful prismatic light moving through textured glass, rich indigo and violet with a warm amber highlight

scenes.text: He'd used changa, a DMT-containing blend. His forum account described an unexpected reunion.
scenes.visual: an open book with pages turning beside a warm reading lamp, a tangible written personal account

scenes.text: A dark room. His wife appeared from behind something resembling a wall, glowing.
scenes.visual: a woman opening a door into a dark interior, practical light illuminating her outline, distant framing with her features obscured

scenes.text: Neither spoke. Yet their shared life returned: falling in love, their children, laughter and tears.
scenes.visual: a family with children playing together in a garden, candid wide shot from behind, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: He wrote that he hadn't repeated it. He wouldn't chase what had happened.
scenes.visual: a cassette tape recorder's stop button being pressed, ending playback of a remembered moment

scenes.text: He felt he'd been able to say goodbye.
scenes.visual: an empty wooden rocking chair gently rocking on a quiet porch in soft daylight

scenes.text: Picture grief as a room inside a house you still have to inhabit.
scenes.visual: a slow walk through an empty house into a sunlit room, visible floor and ordinary walls

scenes.text: You make breakfast. Answer messages. Even laugh. Then a familiar song opens it.
scenes.visual: a vinyl record spinning on a turntable in a living room, the needle playing a familiar song

scenes.text: And everything you never finished saying is sitting exactly where you left it.
scenes.visual: a handwritten letter on a wooden table, loose paper edges stirring in a breeze beside an unused pen

scenes.text: Your ordinary Tuesday has become a doorway. Grief apparently never checks whether you have company.
scenes.visual: an interior door slowly opening to reveal the next room, an ordinary domestic threshold interrupted

scenes.text: His encounter is a personal report. Our room is a metaphor. Neither establishes contact with the dead.
scenes.visual: a magnifying glass inspecting a handwritten journal page on a desk, examining the evidence of a personal account

scenes.text: Something in his account stays with me beyond the question of proof.
scenes.visual: a person holding an old photograph in their hands over a wooden desk, camera focused on the photograph rather than their face

scenes.text: Along that wall of doors, is there one you visit often, and another you avoid?
scenes.visual: a corridor of closed doors receding into the distance, camera slowly approaching the separate doorways

scenes.text: Maybe relief feels like leaving the room empty. As though love needs pain standing guard.
scenes.visual: a padlock being unlocked on a wooden door, the lock and latch clearly visible

scenes.text: Does yours? You don't have to answer quickly.
scenes.visual: sand falling slowly through an hourglass on a quiet table in warm light

scenes.text: He wasn't describing a theory. He was describing his wife, and everything their life had held.
scenes.visual: a hand holding a wedding ring between the fingers, the ring catching soft window light

scenes.text: Afterward, he chose to let the encounter remain something he'd experienced, without repeating it.
scenes.visual: hands gently closing a book and letting it rest on a table, a completed account left intact

scenes.text: A door opened. He didn't spend the rest of his account demanding a key.
scenes.visual: a hand sets a key down on a table and withdraws, leaving the key rather than trying another lock

scenes.text: Back here, your room has ordinary sounds. Air moving. A refrigerator humming. Traffic going past.
scenes.visual: ordinary city traffic passing along a residential street, viewed from a quiet home window

scenes.text: Your feet are touching something solid. Your body is breathing through this sentence.
scenes.visual: bare feet resting on a wooden floor, toes gently moving as a seated person settles into the present room

scenes.text: There's room here for uncertainty, too. A story can move you while its explanation stays unfinished.
scenes.visual: pages of an open book turning in a light breeze, the story remaining open on a table

scenes.text: Perhaps you remember someone now: their laugh, their terrible directions, the particular way they said your name.
scenes.visual: hands turning pages of an old family photo album, holding briefly on shared memories without showing the viewer's face

scenes.text: Whatever you believe about where they are, those memories are meeting you here.
scenes.visual: a curtain moving in warm sunlight through a home window, soft dust and changing light bringing attention back to the room

scenes.text: If your unfinished goodbye had a room, what would you want to say inside it?
scenes.visual: an empty chair beside an open window with a curtain moving in the breeze, a quiet place waiting for the viewer's own words
